identity.name: frosty-raven
rules: score: -0.08007 × (Latest visible DA price, same hour ($/MWh) + (0.4117 $/MWh/index points × (max(US economic policy uncertainty (index points), US economic policy uncertainty (index points)))))
side: DEC if score > 1.3 $/MWh, INC if score < −9.41 $/MWh, else no bid
size: 99% of the location's MW cap × min(1, |score| ÷ 0.5 $/MWh), times the position scale
risk: at most 84% of the daily footprint; pause 1 days after a day losing 0.6%

what_happened: frosty-raven (R101-29627) turned $1,500,000 into $3,199,843 over 2005-04-01 to 2025-03-27 (log growth +0.758, worst fall 8%). On the unseen year 2024-03-28 to 2025-03-27 its log growth was +0.050. Its hardest event was Winter Storm Elliott (-0.5%). It fails G3 overfitting.

caveats: Fees and uplift are labelled estimates until MISO's Market Settlements Rates Factors file is supplied.
MPD is the $12 floor every year (estimate).
The Constraint Management Charge is not modelled.
Price-taker: bids are assumed not to move prices (cap 5 MW per hub-hour, 5 % of typical volume).
L5 peers are not modelled; traders don't interact.
honest_expectation: Virtual bidding is a thin, competitive edge. Published studies that model fees and uplift find small or no profits after costs; a trader that passes these gates on 20 years of history has a better chance than one that doesn't, not a guarantee. Fees and uplift are estimates until MISO's rate file is supplied, the Constraint Management Charge is not modelled, and bids are assumed not to move prices (5 MW cap). Real trading needs MISO registration and collateral.
measured: every P&L, growth, drawdown and gate statistic above, from the downloaded prices and the simulator
assumed: fee and RSG rates; MPD; gate thresholds (95 %, 0.95, 0.5, 50 % loss mandate); the event windows marked as assumptions
